newsitem.title: FRANCE: French insurer CNP hopes for September listing.
newsitem.headline: French insurer CNP hopes for September listing.

text.p: French insurer Caisse Nationale de Prevoyance (CNP), slated for privatisation, hopes to list shares on the Paris stockmarket in September, board chairman Pierre Darnis said on Tuesday.

He told a news conference the government was likely to announce its plans for the group in two or three months and thought it was likely that an operation would be mounted after the August holidays in France.

Darnis said the state would retain majority control. It now holds 42.5 percent of CNP directly, state-owned Caisse des depots holds 30 percent, the French postal service 17.5 percent and state-owned Caisses d'Epargne 10 percent.

Darnis said the state would probably sell around 35 percent of CNP to institutional and individual investors and may at the same time set a capital increase to boost its equity, which was 13 billion francs ($2.3 billion) at the end of last year.
